title: Silithus
body: Silithus is a wasteland of sand, wind and stone in the far southwest of Kalimdor, reached on foot only from Un'Goro. Nearly a thousand years ago the qiraji poured out of their city of Ahn'Qiraj and swept across this desert, until they were sealed behind the Scarab Wall in the south. Now the silithid hives swarm once more, the Cenarion Circle keeps watch from Cenarion Hold, and the Twilight's Hammer camps across the sands.

parts.body: The Circle calls for help: the silithid, too long unchecked, are readying to spread, and volunteers of both factions pour into Cenarion Hold.
The Scarab Gong has sounded. The qiraji pour out upon the desert, resonating crystals burst through the earth and colossi of obsidian stone have risen at the three hives.
The gates of Ahn'Qiraj stand open and the war has been carried inside, where the fighting goes on day and night.

title: Cenarion Hold
body: Cenarion Hold is the fortress of the Cenarion Circle at the heart of Silithus, raised where an old night elf settlement stood, to guard against what lies sealed in the south. Its infantry deal harshly with anyone who spills blood on neutral ground, and a bronze drake circles overhead.

parts.body: The hold has filled for war under Commander Mar'alith, whose beloved Natalia has gone missing after weeks of talking to someone no one else could see. Among the tents a night elf, Baristolth, waits on a promise a thousand years old.
Natalia was found deep in Hive'Regal, become the High Priestess of C'Thun. The grieving commander could only ask what C'Thun was.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Cenarion_Hold (Circle took over the ancient night elven settlement, set up after the war to guard C'Thun; leaders Mar'alith and Vish Kozus)

parts.body: A dwarven geologist unlocked a glyphed prism of the hives and found twenty thousand years of history in it, and a prophecy that, should it come to pass, could mean the end of every future.

title: Southwind Village
body: In eastern Silithus lie the ruins of Southwind Village, once the night elves' base in this land. It fell in the War of the Shifting Sands and the silithid have held it ever since. The tortured spirits of fallen druids and sentinels still wander its streets, and their death wails rouse the hive that has claimed the village tower.

parts.body: Southwind's fall has a name the night elves still mourn. Fandral Staghelm ordered his son Valstann to defend the village, and Valstann died there on the day it fell.

title: Hive'Regal
body: Hive'Regal is the southern hive of Silithus, haunt of slavemakers, spitfires and hive lords, and like its sister hives of Ashi and Zora it guards a crystal carved with qiraji glyphs. Deep in its tunnels a Cenarion scout creeps close enough to the insects to go unnoticed, though he would not advise anyone to try it.

parts.body: Somewhere in its depths is Natalia Mar'alith. The dwarves saw her run into the hive after her madness took her, and not one insect tried to bar her way.
sources: zone_areas 2744: Hive'Regal Slavemaker, Spitfire, Hive Lord, Ambusher, Burrower, Lapress 14473, Krug Skullsplit 15612, Merok, Kirika's camp 17079

parts.body: The war has reached the hive: the Colossus of Regal has risen, and a great resonating crystal of the qiraji has broken through the sand before it.

title: The Crystal Vale
body: In the far northwest of Silithus lies the Crystal Vale, ruled by elementals of earth and air, and within it the ravaged remains of a Twilight's Hammer camp. A lone human, Highlord Demitrian, keeps vigil there, and to those who pass he says only this: look to this ravaged field and know the power that the elements hold.

parts.body: A diary decoded from the camp's clay tablets tells of pilgrims who raised a wind stone to speak with their masters, and readied the rituals to summon Baron Kazum himself. There the diary ends.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Crystal_Vale (far northwestern corner, earth and air elementals, thorium, Ravaged Twilight Camp, Demitrian)

parts.body: Demitrian serves Thunderaan, Prince of Air, betrayed in the Elemental Sundering by Ragnaros's lieutenants Geddon and Garr, struck down by the Firelord and fed upon; what remained was sealed in a talisman, broken in two.

title: Bronzebeard Encampment
body: In the southern hills of Silithus, east of the Scarab Wall, the dwarves of Brann Bronzebeard's expedition have made camp to search the hives for lost artifacts; between the four of them, monkey included, they speak thirty-eight languages. Brann himself has gone missing again, and his companions' pleas to Ironforge for an army go unanswered.

parts.body: A letter in Brann's hand tells of a great battle between a titan and an Old God, a bona fide one, and of an ancient tunnel into Ahn'Qiraj that he meant to take.

title: The Scarab Wall
body: In the far southwest of Silithus runs the Scarab Wall, raised at the end of the War of the Shifting Sands to seal the qiraji and their silithid within Ahn'Qiraj. In it stand the gates of the fortress city, bound for a thousand years by great roots and glowing runes, and before them rises the Scarab Dais. Near the wall lies a single crystalline tear, left as a symbol of the great losses of that war.

parts.body: Those who gaze into the tear feel a sorrow so heavy they fear they might die of it, and in its depths a long forgotten memory of the old war stirs.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Scarab_Wall (molded from the sand, bronze dragonflight barrier many times taller)

parts.body: The gong has been rung. Roots, runes and the great doors gave way, and the qiraji came out to meet the world.
Now nothing bars the way through the wall, and the Circle's allies carry the war into the ruined city and on toward the temple beyond.
